newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Biplane crashes in Russian north, 13 killed.
newsitem.headline: Biplane crashes in Russian north, 13 killed.

text.p: Thirteen people were killed when an antiquated Antonov An-2 biplane crashed in northern Russia on Thursday, Interfax news agency said quoting officials at the Emergencies Ministry.

The only survivor of the crash, near the village of Bolshaya Pyssa in the semi-autonomous Komi region, appeared to be the co-pilot. He was badly injured, Interfax said. The pilot of the single-engined craft and all 12 passengers were dead.

An Emergencies Ministry spokesman later confirmed the report. He pinpointed the crash site 250 km (160 miles) northwest of Syktyvkar, the regional capital, which would put it about 200 km (120 miles) south of the Arctic Circle.

The plane had been attempting to take off when it came down and exploded. The co-pilot was thrown clear, a regional official told Reuters. He had no details on weather conditions in the area. Winter is setting in in northern Russia, bringing snow.
During a blizzard three weeks ago, a Yakovlev Yak-40 passenger jet missed the runway at Khanty-Mansiisk in Siberia and five people were killed.

Air safety standards in the former Soviet Union have been severely criticised in recent years. Problems were spotlighted this week when a Kazakh cargo plane was involved in the world's worst mid-air collision over India on Tuesday. Some 350 people were killed.
